references.text: Luke 22:22 contains two main themes with rich cross-references: (1) that the Son of Man goes away "as it has been determined" (God's predestined plan), and (2) the woe pronounced on the one who betrays him.

[ref:Isa 53:10|Isaiah 53:10] – The Lord’s will was to crush his suffering servant, pointing to the divine plan behind Jesus’ suffering and death, as "it has been determined" (ὡρισμένον) in [ref:Lk 22:22|Luke 22:22].
[ref:Ps 41:10|Psalms 41:10] – "My close friend, whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me." A prophetic text about betrayal by a close friend, which Jesus applies to Judas.

[ref:Acts 2:23|Acts of the Apostles 2:23] – Peter explains that Jesus was handed over "according to God’s set plan and foreknowledge," a direct parallel to the Son of Man going away "as it has been determined."

[ref:Acts 4:27-28|Acts of the Apostles 4:27-28] – The believers confess that everything that happened to Jesus—the actions of Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles, and Israel—was predestined by God’s hand and plan.

[ref:Matt 26:24|Matthew 26:24] – Parallel passage: "The Son of Man goes away as it is written about him, but woe to that man who betrays the Son of Man! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born."
[ref:Mark 14:21|Mark 14:21] – Parallel passage in Mark: "The Son of Man goes away as it is written about him, but woe to that man who betrays the Son of Man!"
[ref:John 13:18|John 13:18] – Jesus says that Scripture had to be fulfilled: "He who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me," linking the betrayal to God’s predestined plan.

[ref:John 17:12|John 17:12] – In his high priestly prayer, Jesus states that none of the disciples were lost except "the son of destruction, so that Scripture might be fulfilled," confirming divine determination.

[ref:Lk 24:26-27|Luke 24:26-27] – The risen Jesus explains that the Messiah "had to suffer these things" and enter his glory, interpreting all the Scriptures concerning him—confirming that his suffering was determined.

[ref:Acts 1:16|Acts of the Apostles 1:16] – Peter says that "Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold through David about Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus," confirming the prophetic determination.

[ref:Isa 53:3|Isaiah 53:3] – The prophecy of the suffering servant who is despised and forsaken by people, providing background for why the Son of Man "goes away" through suffering in accordance with God’s plan.
